challenged_source.scope: Corollary 5.2 proof step conditioning on all pair variables except U_I,V_J and then reusing marginal density caps for the active conditional variables

claim: After conditioning on the conjugate sum/difference variables, each active U_i or V_j still has one-dimensional density cap at most one.
counterexample: For iid X,X' uniform on [0,1], U=X+X', V=X-X'. For |v|<1, U conditional on V=v is uniform on [|v|,2-|v|], so its density cap equals 1/[2(1-|v|)] and diverges as |v| tends to 1.
safe_replacement: For general f<=1, ||p_{U|V=v}||_infinity <= 1/[2 p_V(v)] and symmetrically for V|U. Applying the bilinear lemma after conditioning introduces products of int p_U^(2/3) and int p_V^(2/3), which are unbounded over admissible laws. Retain the earlier original-coordinate square-crosspacket Plancherel theorem instead; it proves the branch without conditioning conjugate pair variables.
